entry.title: Understanding Decoder-Only Transformers Part 1: Masked Self-Attention
entry.summary:
Decoder-Only Transformers
In this article, we will explore decoder-only transformers. Decoder-only transformers are a specific type of transformer architecture used in systems like ChatGPT. Decoder-only transformers use a mechanism called masked self-attention. Masked self-attention works by measuring how similar each word is to itself and to the words that come before it in the sentence. For example: “The pizza came out of the oven and it tasted good.” When processing the word “pizza”, masked self-attention only considers the preceding word “The”. Unlike standard self-attention, masked self-attention does not allow a word to look at future words. It can only attend to the current word and the words that come before it. Because of this, it is also called an auto-regressive method. An auto-regressive method is a way of predicting values step by step, where each prediction depends on the previous outputs. The model uses its past predictions as input to generate the next output It builds the final result one step at a time Each step depends on what was generated before it, not what comes after We will explore this concept in more detail in the next article. entry.title: The 8-Week Technical Interview Prep System That Actually Works (for Busy Engineers)
entry.summary: Most technical interview prep fails for one reason: people optimize for volume, not system. You can solve 200 problems and still underperform in interviews if you don’t train timing, communication, and feedback loops. This is the 8-week framework I use for engineers who are preparing while working full-time. Who this is for Doing random problems with no sequencing Problem-solving accuracy Take 2 timed coding mocks Weeks 3–5: Core build Weekly structure: 3 coding sessions (timed + postmortem) Don’t just solve — explain choices out loud Start from requirements and constraints One story should map to multiple question variants Run 2–3 full mock loops (coding + design + behavioral) Week 8: Final polish Company-specific prep (question style, role expectations, domain) Mon: Coding (75 min) Readiness scorecard (simple but effective) Coding accuracy under time Common failure modes (and fixes) “I’m good at coding but weak in design rounds.” “Behavioral feels vague and repetitive.” “I’m burning out.” Final thought If you run a structured 8-week loop with clear feedback, your confidence and outcomes improve dramatically. If helpful, I can share a free one-page version of this framework with a weekly checklist.
